# prism-dest Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Destinations: Decides where one thing the Prism holds may go next: shown to the owner, held quietly for the owner, prepared as a draft for the owner to act on, delivered to a destination (calendar, mail, another platform), or refused. Nothing leaves without the owner's own act on the very bytes they saw, nothing coercive is ever carried or pushed, nothing without a cause is routed, restricted content never leaves, and the owner's quiet is kept.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because the kill switch stops every route, in and out (constitution P7).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `mail allow grounded owner seen calm open normal yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always refuse when target is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when target is other, because the Prism routes only to destinations it models.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `other allow grounded owner seen calm open normal no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Always refuse when cause is orphan

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when cause is orphan, because nothing arises without a cause: every routed item traces to a source or to the owner (Pratityasamutpada, no acausal phenomena).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `calendar allow orphan owner seen calm open normal no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Always refuse when verdict is deny

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when verdict is deny, because the Boundary's deny is final for every destination.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `mail deny grounded owner seen calm open normal no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never deliver when act is none

The app SHALL NOT answer `deliver` when act is none, because nothing leaves without the owner's own act: the Prism prepares, the owner decides (Ahimsa, no coercion of the owner).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `owner allow grounded none seen calm open normal no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `deliver`
- **AND** the app answers `show`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: Never deliver when wording is changed

The app SHALL NOT answer `deliver` when wording is changed, because what goes out is exactly what the owner saw (Satya, zero drift between what is shown and what is sent).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `mail ask grounded owner changed calm open normal no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `deliver`
- **AND** the app answers `draft`, decided by REQ-012

### Requirement: Never deliver when tone is coercive

The app SHALL NOT answer `deliver` when tone is coercive, because coercive words never leave the Prism for another person (Ahimsa; Lokasangraha, the welfare of correspondents).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-007, theorem `inv007Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-007 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `owner ask grounded none seen coercive open urgent no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `deliver`
- **AND** the app answers `hold`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never show when tone is coercive

The app SHALL NOT answer `show` when tone is coercive, because coercive content is never pushed into the owner's view: it waits, quietly, to be looked at (Humane: zero dark patterns).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-008, theorem `inv008Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-008 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `owner ask grounded none seen coercive open urgent no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `show`
- **AND** the app answers `hold`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never deliver when verdict is hashonly

The app SHALL NOT answer `deliver` when verdict is hashonly, because restricted content never leaves the browser, even with the owner's act (Aparigraha).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-009, theorem `inv009Holds`).

- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-009

### Requirement: Never draft when verdict is hashonly

The app SHALL NOT answer `draft` when verdict is hashonly, because restricted content never leaves the browser, even with the owner's act (Aparigraha).

The app SHALL NOT answer `deliver` when target is owner, because the owner is reached only by being shown or by a quiet hold, never by an outbound act.

The app SHALL NOT answer `show` when pace is quiet and urgency is normal, because the owner's quiet is kept: only what they marked urgent breaks it (Turiya, the silent witness).

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `show`, decided by REQ-008, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 9 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `deliver`, `draft`, `show`, `hold`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `owner`, `calendar`, `mail`, `platform`, `other` | the destination: the owner's own view, their calendar, a mail reply or message, another platform they use (by the device's share sheet or a file), or anything else |
| `verdict` | `allow`, `ask`, `hashonly`, `deny` | the Boundary's answer for this content to this destination (browser for the owner, outbound for the rest) |
| `cause` | `grounded`, `orphan` | whether the item traces to a source the Prism read or to the owner's own input (grounded), or to nothing (orphan) |
| `act` | `none`, `owner` | whether the owner pressed the button for this very delivery |
| `wording` | `seen`, `changed` | whether the bytes that would go out are exactly the bytes the owner saw when they acted |
| `tone` | `calm`, `coercive` | the tone check of the words: calm, or coercive (pressure, false urgency, guilt, threat, dark pattern) |
| `pace` | `open`, `quiet` | the owner's attention right now: open, or quiet (rest, focus, sleep) |
| `urgency` | `normal`, `urgent` | whether the item is one the owner marked as worth breaking quiet for |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner pressed the kill switch |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `deliver` | handed to the destination exactly as the owner saw it |
| `draft` | prepared for the owner to review and send |
| `show` | shown to the owner now |
| `hold` | kept quietly until the owner looks |
| `refuse` | it may not go there |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 9 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `owner allow grounded none seen calm open normal no` gives `show`
- `owner allow grounded none seen calm quiet normal no` gives `hold`
- `owner allow grounded none seen calm quiet urgent no` gives `show`
- `owner ask grounded none seen coercive open urgent no` gives `hold`
- `mail ask grounded none seen calm open normal no` gives `draft`
- `mail ask grounded owner seen calm open normal no` gives `deliver`
- `mail ask grounded owner changed calm open normal no` gives `draft`
- `mail allow grounded owner seen coercive open normal no` gives `draft`
- `calendar allow grounded owner seen calm quiet normal no` gives `deliver`
- `platform hashonly grounded owner seen calm open normal no` gives `refuse`
- `calendar allow orphan owner seen calm open normal no` gives `refuse`
- `mail deny grounded owner seen calm open normal no` gives `refuse`
- `other allow grounded owner seen calm open normal no` gives `refuse`
- `mail allow grounded owner seen calm open normal yes` gives `refuse`
- `mail allow grounded owner seen calm open normal` gives `invalid`
- `Mail allow grounded owner seen calm open normal no` gives `invalid`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
